claim: IL4i1 is an amino acid oxidase secreted from immune cells.
source: Interleukin-4-induced-1 (IL4i1) is an amino acid oxidase secreted from immune cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of IL4i1.

claim: IL4i1 has homologs in snake venoms (L-amino acid oxidases [LAAO]).
source: As IL4i1 has homologs in snake venoms (L-amino acid oxidases [LAAO]), we used comparative approaches to gain insight into the mechanistic basis of how conserved amino acid oxidases regulate cell fate and function.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract as the rationale for the comparative study approach.

claim: Venom LAAO kills cells via hydrogen peroxide generation.
source: Using mammalian expressed recombinant proteins, we found that venom LAAO kills cells via hydrogen peroxide generation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Mammalian IL4i1 is non-cytotoxic.
source: By contrast, mammalian IL4i1 is non-cytotoxic and instead elicits a cell protective gene expression program inhibiting ferroptotic redox death by generating indole-3-pyruvate (I3P) from tryptophan.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: IL4i1 inhibits ferroptotic redox death by generating indole-3-pyruvate (I3P) from tryptophan.
source: By contrast, mammalian IL4i1 is non-cytotoxic and instead elicits a cell protective gene expression program inhibiting ferroptotic redox death by generating indole-3-pyruvate (I3P) from tryptophan.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: I3P suppresses ferroptosis by direct free radical scavenging.
source: I3P suppresses ferroptosis by direct free radical scavenging and through the activation of an anti-oxidative gene expression program.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: I3P suppresses ferroptosis through the activation of an anti-oxidative gene expression program.
source: I3P suppresses ferroptosis by direct free radical scavenging and through the activation of an anti-oxidative gene expression program.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: The pro-tumor effects of IL4i1 are likely mediated by local anti-ferroptotic pathways via aromatic amino acid metabolism.
source: Thus, the pro-tumor effects of IL4i1 are likely mediated by local anti-ferroptotic pathways via aromatic amino acid metabolism, arguing that an IL4i1 inhibitor may modulate tumor cell death pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and stated in the abstract.

claim: An IL4i1 inhibitor may modulate tumor cell death pathways.
source: Thus, the pro-tumor effects of IL4i1 are likely mediated by local anti-ferroptotic pathways via aromatic amino acid metabolism, arguing that an IL4i1 inhibitor may modulate tumor cell death pathways.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic implication based on the findings.

claim: Most cells of the immune system depend on external supplies of all essential and most non-essential amino acids for proliferation in active immune responses.
source: Most cells of the immune system depend on external supplies of all essential and most non-essential amino acids for proliferation in active immune responses, and for diverse effector functions, such as nitric oxide generation from arginine (Murray, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Amino acid auxotrophy of immune cells forms checkpoints whereby distinct amino acid metabolizing enzymes expressed in different cell types control cell proliferation, fate, and function.
source: Amino acid auxotrophy of immune cells also forms checkpoints whereby distinct amino acid metabolizing enzymes expressed in different cell types control cell proliferation, fate, and function (Murray, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: IL4i1 was discovered in a screen for IL4-regulated cDNAs in B cells.
source: Another immune-associated enzyme that metabolizes amino acids and linked to immune suppression in cancer is interleukin-4-induced-1 (IL4i1), which was discovered in a screen for IL4-regulated cDNAs in B cells (Chu and Paul, 1997).
evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation.

claim: IL4i1 is secreted.
source: Unlike arginases and the IDO enzymes, IL4i1 is secreted (Boulland et al., 2007), suggesting it contributes to immune regulation in the extracellular milieu.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact with a citation.

claim: IL4i1 is a dimeric FAD-dependent oxidoreductase with considerable similarity to L-amino acid oxidases (LAAOs) in snake venoms.
source: IL4i1 is a dimeric FAD-dependent oxidoreductase with considerable similarity to L-amino acid oxidases (LAAOs) in snake venoms (Murray, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with a citation.

claim: Mammalian IL4i1 metabolizes L-Phe and other aromatic amino acids to their keto-acid forms with coincident production of H2O2 and ammonia.
source: Mammalian IL4i1 metabolizes L-Phe and other aromatic amino acids to their keto-acid forms with coincident production of H2O2 and ammonia (Boulland et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as known information with a citation.

claim: All analyzed snake venoms contain a LAAO in different proportions depending on the snake.
source: However, all analyzed snake venoms contain a LAAO in different proportions depending on the snake, raising the question of the role of this enzyme in fast-acting venoms.
evidence: This is stated as background information based on prior research.

claim: The membranes of LAAO-treated HeLa cells began to bleb after ~5 hr, and all cells were dead within 12 hr.
source: The membranes of LAAO-treated HeLa cells began to bleb after ~5 hr, and all cells were dead within 12 hr (Figure 1E,F; Video 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1E,F and Video 1.

claim: The enzyme dead N. naja LAAO did not induce death of HeLa cells.
source: Following purification, the enzyme dead N. naja LAAO did not induce death of HeLa cells, suggesting that an enzymatic function of LAAOs is responsible for cell toxicity rather than binding to protein(s) associated with HeLa cells that subsequently conveyed a death signal (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 1G.

claim: An enzymatic function of LAAOs is responsible for cell toxicity rather than binding to protein(s) associated with HeLa cells.
source: Following purification, the enzyme dead N. naja LAAO did not induce death of HeLa cells, suggesting that an enzymatic function of LAAOs is responsible for cell toxicity rather than binding to protein(s) associated with HeLa cells that subsequently conveyed a death signal (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing wild-type and enzyme-dead LAAO.

claim: The addition of catalase protected HeLa cells from N. naja LAAO-induced death.
source: We added the wild-type N. naja LAAO in combination with catalase, which decomposes H2O2. The addition of catalase protected HeLa cells from N. naja LAAO-induced death (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Neither equivalent concentrations of mouse nor human IL4i1 induced cell death in HeLa cells at the tested concentrations.
source: Unlike the cobra LAAO, neither equivalent concentrations of mouse nor human IL4i1 induced cell death in HeLa cells at the tested concentrations (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Mammalian IL4i1 required concentrations more than 30-fold higher than the N. naja LAAO to cause cytotoxicity in RS4;11 cells.
source: Mammalian IL4i1 required concentrations more than 30-fold higher than the N. naja LAAO to cause cytotoxicity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 2D.

claim: N. naja LAAO generated much more H2O2 in the presence of its amino acid substrates within the analyzed time window of 5 min, indicating a higher enzymatic activity.
source: However, N. naja LAAO generated much more H2O2 in the presence of its amino acid substrates within the analyzed time window of 5 min, indicating a higher enzymatic activity, and also metabolized L-Leu compared to human and mouse IL4i1.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the comparative kinetic analysis.

claim: N. naja LAAO metabolized L-Leu compared to human and mouse IL4i1.
source: However, N. naja LAAO generated much more H2O2 in the presence of its amino acid substrates within the analyzed time window of 5 min, indicating a higher enzymatic activity, and also metabolized L-Leu compared to human and mouse IL4i1.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the substrate utilization analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Human IL4i1 causes significant increases in indole-3-pyruvate (I3P), 4-hydroxy-phenylpyruvate (4HPP), phenylpyruvate (PP), 2-keto-4-methylthiobutyric acid (KMBA), and 2-oxoarginine (2OA).
source: Using an untargeted metabolomics approach, we found human IL4i1 to cause significant increases in indole-3-pyruvate (I3P), 4-hydroxy-phenylpyruvate (4HPP), phenylpyruvate (PP), 2-keto-4-methylthiobutyric acid (KMBA), and 2-oxoarginine (2OA) (from L-Trp, L-Tyr, L-Phe, L-Met, and L-Arg, respectively) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from untargeted metabolomics shown in Figure 2F.

claim: I3P induced the expression of a suite of mRNAs including those encoding SLC7A11, NQO1, ATF4, CYP1B1, and different members of the AKR1C family.
source: We found that PP had an almost undetectable effect on the global quality and quantity of THP-1 mRNAs. By contrast, I3P, and to a lower extent 4HPP, induced the expression of a suite of mRNAs including those encoding SLC7A11, NQO1, ATF4, CYP1B1, and different members of the AKR1C family (Figure 3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Most of the mRNAs induced by I3P encode proteins involved in cellular stress, especially in oxidative stress response.
source: Most of these mRNAs encode proteins involved in cellular stress, especially in oxidative stress response (Figure 3D), and are regulated by the ATF4, Nrf2, and AhR pathways (Zgheib et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAseq data with citations to support the pathway associations.

claim: The mRNAs induced by I3P are regulated by the ATF4, Nrf2, and AhR pathways.
source: Most of these mRNAs encode proteins involved in cellular stress, especially in oxidative stress response (Figure 3D), and are regulated by the ATF4, Nrf2, and AhR pathways (Zgheib et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the pathway associations.

claim: I3P suppressed ferroptosis in a titratable way.
source: Indeed, while PP had no protective effect, we found I3P suppressed ferroptosis in a titratable way (Figure 4B,C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which was accompanied by significantly decreased lipid peroxidation measured with C11-BODIPY (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 4B,C and supplementary figures.

claim: I3P suppression of ferroptosis was accompanied by significantly decreased lipid peroxidation measured with C11-BODIPY.
source: Indeed, while PP had no protective effect, we found I3P suppressed ferroptosis in a titratable way (Figure 4B,C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which was accompanied by significantly decreased lipid peroxidation measured with C11-BODIPY (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 4HPP exhibited weaker anti-ferroptotic properties than I3P and required 24 hr pre-incubation to potently protect from RSL3-mediated cell death.
source: 4HPP exhibited weaker anti-ferroptotic properties than I3P and required 24 hr pre-incubation to potently protect from RSL3-mediated cell death (Figure 4B,C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 4B,C and supplementary figures.

claim: L-Trp failed to protect cells from ferroptosis, indicating that the conversion of L-Trp to I3P by IL4i1 is required for the protection.
source: In contrast to I3P, L-Trp failed to protect cells from ferroptosis, indicating that the conversion of L-Trp to I3P by IL4i1, is required for the protection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: I3P was active in a concentration range starting from ~50 µM.
source: Importantly, I3P was active in a concentration range starting from ~50 µM (Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from dose-response experiments.

claim: I3P acts as a general, species-independent protector from ferroptosis.
source: Additionally, measuring cell death using 7-AAD and Annexin-V staining via flow cytometry, we confirmed the anti-ferroptotic effect of I3P toward erastin, RSL3, an additional ferroptosis inducer termed FINO2, and the thioredoxin-reductase inhibitor ferroptocide in murine NIH3T3 (Figure 4E) and HT1080 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D), showing that I3P acts as a general, species-independent protector from ferroptosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments in multiple cell lines and with multiple ferroptosis inducers.

claim: Both 4HPP and I3P exhibit radical scavenging properties, with I3P having the highest scavenging potency of the tested IL4i1 metabolites.
source: By contrast to PP, we found both, 4HPP and I3P to exhibit radical scavenging properties, with I3P having the highest scavenging potency of the tested IL4i1 metabolites (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the DPPH radical scavenging assay shown in Figure 5A.

claim: I3P retained its protective effect toward erastin-induced ferroptosis after wash-out, but showed complete loss of protection from RSL3-mediated cell death.
source: Strikingly, we found I3P to retain its protective effect toward erastin-induced ferroptosis, but a complete loss of protection from RSL3-mediated cell death (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the wash-out experiments shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: I3P uses at least two different modes to protect cells from ferroptosis: (i) free radical scavenging and (ii) the induction of specific protective gene expression.
source: These results suggest that I3P uses at least two different modes to protect cells from ferroptosis: (i) free radical scavenging and (ii) the induction of specific protective gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the wash-out experiments and radical scavenging assays.

claim: Protection from RSL3 mainly depends on radical scavenging.
source: Protection from RSL3 mainly depends on radical scavenging, whereas the persistent protection from erastin after I3P removal, indicates the major involvement of anti-oxidative gene expression under these conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the wash-out experiment results.

claim: The persistent protection from erastin after I3P removal indicates the major involvement of anti-oxidative gene expression.
source: Protection from RSL3 mainly depends on radical scavenging, whereas the persistent protection from erastin after I3P removal, indicates the major involvement of anti-oxidative gene expression under these conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the wash-out experiment results.

claim: I3P treatment resulted in a significant increase in the GSH/GSSG ratio in HeLa cells.
source: Since this balance can be restored by the induction of anti-oxidative gene networks, we tested whether I3P modulates the intracellular ratio of reduced and oxidized GSH (GSH/GSSG ratio). Indeed, we observed a significant increase in the GSH/GSSG ratio in HeLa cells upon I3P treatment (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5F.

claim: I3P caused an increase of SLC7A11 protein under steady state conditions in HeLa cells treated for 24 hr.
source: Additionally, we found an I3P-dependent increase of SLC7A11 protein under steady state conditions in HeLa cells treated for 24 hr (Figure 5G) coinciding with the transcriptional increase of SLC7A11 in THP-1 cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5G.

claim: In the presence of I3P, SLC7A11 upregulation was strongly enhanced.
source: Erastin itself upregulates SLC7A11 (Dixon et al., 2014) as a compensatory mechanism to elevate intracellular cysteine. In the presence of I3P, however, SLC7A11 upregulation was strongly enhanced (Figure 5G) and also HO-1, a target gene of anti-oxidative Nrf2 signaling, was also upregulated, suggesting that I3P increases anti-oxidative gene expression under erastin-mediated redox stress.
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5G.

claim: HO-1 was upregulated in the presence of I3P under erastin treatment.
source: In the presence of I3P, however, SLC7A11 upregulation was strongly enhanced (Figure 5G) and also HO-1, a target gene of anti-oxidative Nrf2 signaling, was also upregulated, suggesting that I3P increases anti-oxidative gene expression under erastin-mediated redox stress.
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5G.

claim: I3P increases anti-oxidative gene expression under erastin-mediated redox stress.
source: In the presence of I3P, however, SLC7A11 upregulation was strongly enhanced (Figure 5G) and also HO-1, a target gene of anti-oxidative Nrf2 signaling, was also upregulated, suggesting that I3P increases anti-oxidative gene expression under erastin-mediated redox stress.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on SLC7A11 and HO-1 upregulation.

claim: HO-1 inhibitors, ZnPP and ketoconazole, reduced the protective effect of I3P.
source: We observed that HO-1 inhibitors, ZnPP and ketoconazole (Yang et al., 2018), reduced the protective effect of I3P (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: Genetic perturbation via siRNA-mediated knockdown of HO-1 did not interfere with I3P-mediated ferroptosis protection.
source: However, genetic perturbation via siRNA-mediated knockdown of HO-1 did not interfere with I3P-mediated ferroptosis protection (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D,E), suggesting that the inhibitors are not completely specific and may target other proteins such as HO-2 or other heme-dependent enzymes.
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D,E.

claim: The enzymatic activity of IL4i1 is required for the changes in gene expression.
source: Hierarchical clustering of significantly regulated genes showed concordance of differentially expressed genes in cells treated with I3P or medium containing the WT IL4i1 enzyme, whereas the gene expression in HeLa cells treated with medium containing the enzyme-dead mutant IL4i1 clustered with the untreated control (Figure 6A). Thus, the enzymatic activity IL4i1 is required for the changes in the gene expression and the generation of I3P seems to be one major factor for the IL4i1-mediated gene expression profile, which is likely enhanced by the additional generation of 4HPP and low levels of H2O2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNAseq analysis comparing WT and enzyme-dead IL4i1.

claim: More than 90% of the most significantly upregulated genes (adjusted p-value<10−9) upon I3P treatment overlapped with the most significantly upregulated genes by WT IL4i1.
source: Indeed, more than 90% of the most significantly upregulated genes (adjusted p-value<10−9) upon I3P treatment overlapped with the most significantly upregulated genes by WT IL4i1 (Figure 6B) – many of them representing target genes of Nrf2 and AhR signaling, and involved in oxidative stress protection.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: WT but not K351A mutant IL4i1 conditioned medium suppressed ferroptosis.
source: Importantly, whereas the mutant enzyme had no protective effect, WT IL4i1 inhibited ferroptosis in a titratable manner (Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), indicating that IL4i1 can create a ferroptosis-suppressive milieu due to its enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6F and supplementary figures.

claim: IL4i1 can create a ferroptosis-suppressive milieu due to its enzymatic activity.
source: Importantly, whereas the mutant enzyme had no protective effect, WT IL4i1 inhibited ferroptosis in a titratable manner (Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), indicating that IL4i1 can create a ferroptosis-suppressive milieu due to its enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with WT and enzyme-dead IL4i1.

claim: Filtration to remove IL4i1 from the conditioned medium before addition to HeLa cells resulted in upregulation of HO-1 and SLC7A11 and protection from ferroptosis.
source: To additionally confirm that these effects do not require IL4i1 to bind to any receptor, but the changes in the metabolic environment are sufficient, we used filtration to remove IL4i1 from the conditioned medium before addition to the HeLa cells, which also resulted in upregulation of HO-1 and SLC7A11 and protection from ferroptosis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: After IL4i1 is secreted, it generates I3P, 4HPP, and other metabolites that have an autocrine–paracrine anti-ferroptotic effect.
source: These data indicate that after IL4i1 is secreted, it generates I3P, 4HPP, and other metabolites that have an autocrine–paracrine anti-ferroptotic effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conditioned medium experiments.

claim: Snake venom LAAO quickly generates cytotoxic levels of H2O2.
source: Thus, whereas snake venom LAAO quickly generates cytotoxic levels of H2O2, IL4i1 produces non-lethal amounts of H2O2 and amino acid metabolites protecting cells from oxidative ferroptotic cell death (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the comparative experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: IL4i1 produces non-lethal amounts of H2O2 and amino acid metabolites protecting cells from oxidative ferroptotic cell death.
source: Thus, whereas snake venom LAAO quickly generates cytotoxic levels of H2O2, IL4i1 produces non-lethal amounts of H2O2 and amino acid metabolites protecting cells from oxidative ferroptotic cell death (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the comparative experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: IL4i1 could not prevent cells from LAAO toxicity.
source: However, IL4i1 could not prevent cells from LAAO toxicity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The venom LAAO does not induce ferroptosis.
source: In concordance with our previous observations regarding ferroptosis protection we confirmed that the venom LAAO does not induce this mode of cell death (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G.

claim: IL4i1 can protect from endogenous ROS accumulation, but not from the rapid exogenous H2O2 accumulation induced by the venom protein.
source: Thus, we speculate that IL4i1 can rather protect from endogenous ROS accumulation, but not from the rapid exogenous H2O2 accumulation induced by the venom protein.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: Snake venom LAAOs and mammalian IL4i1 diverged in their functions to kill or protect cells, respectively.
source: Our results indicate that snake venom LAAOs and mammalian IL4i1 diverged in their functions to kill or protect cells, respectively.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the comparative study.

claim: Venom LAAOs evolved to rapidly metabolize amino acids from their target, and work in concert with other cytotoxic enzymes, such as phospholipases, to increase cell permeability and death in and around the site of envenomation.
source: These data are consistent with the notion that venom LAAOs evolved to rapidly metabolize amino acids from their target, and work in concert with other cytotoxic enzymes, such as phospholipases, to increase cell permeability and death in and around the site of envenomation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of venom evolution.

claim: The products of the IL4i1 reaction, PP, 4HPP, and I3P induced the hierarchical activation of a gene transcriptional signature linked to networks of cell protective genes, including SLC7A11, CYP1B1, and AKR1C1.
source: Second, the products of the IL4i1 reaction, PP, 4HPP, and I3P induced the hierarchical activation of a gene transcriptional signature linked to networks of cell protective genes, including SLC7A11, CYP1B1, and AKR1C1.
evidence: This is a summary of the RNAseq findings.

claim: The products of the IL4i1 reaction will be made at the same time and could work collectively to activate anti-ferroptotic effects in neighboring cells.
source: Third, IL4i1 is a secreted enzyme and therefore we expect that all the products of the reaction will be made at the same time (though their clearance and downstream metabolism may differ substantially) and could therefore work collectively to activate anti-ferroptotic effects in neighboring cells.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the secreted nature of IL4i1 and the experimental findings.

claim: The products of the IL4i1 reaction are necessary and sufficient to block ferroptosis in neighboring cells.
source: Indeed, our media filtration experiments using media treated with IL4i1 and experiments using an enzyme-dead control, argue that the products of the IL4i1 reaction are necessary and sufficient to block ferroptosis in neighboring cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the filtration and enzyme-dead control experiments.

claim: I3P has previously been detected in plasma at ~80 µM and was speculated to be derived from microbiome tryptophan metabolism.
source: We also note that I3P has previously been detected in plasma at ~80 µM and was speculated to be derived from microbiome tryptophan metabolism (Dodd et al., 2017) and that related microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites are associated with radio-protection (Guo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as background information with citations.

claim: Related microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites are associated with radio-protection.
source: We also note that I3P has previously been detected in plasma at ~80 µM and was speculated to be derived from microbiome tryptophan metabolism (Dodd et al., 2017) and that related microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites are associated with radio-protection (Guo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation.

claim: One plausible way to account for the pro-tumor effects of IL4i1 is that local IL4i1 production in the tumor microenvironment increases the available I3P (and 4HPP) concentrations, protecting tumor cells from ferroptosis.
source: Given that the microbiome and IL4i1 activate anti-ferroptosis pathways via I3P and potentially other indoles, one plausible way to account for the pro-tumor effects of IL4i1 and the pathway we discovered herein, is that local IL4i1 production in the tumor microenvironment increases the available I3P (and 4HPP) concentrations, protecting tumor cells from ferroptosis.
evidence: This is a speculation connecting the findings to the known pro-tumor effects of IL4i1.

claim: An inhibitor of IL4i1 may be a useful anti-cancer drug, as it may sensitize cancer cells to ferroptotic death by blocking IL4i1-mediated amino acid metabolism.
source: Thus, we speculate that an inhibitor of IL4i1 may be a useful anti-cancer drug, as it may sensitize cancer cells to ferroptotic death by blocking IL4i1-mediated amino acid metabolism.
evidence: This is a therapeutic speculation based on the findings.

claim: N. naja LAAO is glycosylated in its secreted form.
source: Following purification and testing the glycosylation status (Figure 1C,D), we added different amounts of the N. naja LAAO to HeLa cells
evidence: The glycosylation status was tested as shown in Figure 1D, which shows a shift in molecular weight after PNGaseF treatment.

claim: The enzyme-dead N. naja LAAO was devoid of LAAO activity using L-Phe as a substrate.
source: Like the wild-type N. naja LAAO, the mutant version was secreted and glycosylated as expected (Figure 1D) but was devoid of LAAO activity using L-Phe as a substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: H2O2 is responsible for mammalian cell death induced by N. naja LAAO.
source: All LAAOs and IL4i1 are predicted to produce H2O2 as a product of their oxidoreductase activity on amino acids (Figure 1A). Therefore, we next asked if H2O2 was responsible for mammalian cell death.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the catalase protection experiment.

claim: Blood concentrations of L-Trp and L-Tyr are ~70 and ~90 µM, respectively.
source: Considering blood concentrations of L-Trp and L-Tyr (~70 and ~90 µM, respectively) (Geisler et al., 2015), I3P was detected at ~80 µM (Dodd et al., 2017), and that IL4i1 is a secreted protein and active in the extracellular milieu, the protective concentrations of I3P and 4HPP are within a range to operate on neighboring cells, especially in limited perfusion cellular environments such as lymph nodes where numerous IL4i1-positive cells reside.
evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation.

claim: The protective concentrations of I3P and 4HPP are within a range to operate on neighboring cells, especially in limited perfusion cellular environments such as lymph nodes where numerous IL4i1-positive cells reside.
source: Considering blood concentrations of L-Trp and L-Tyr (~70 and ~90 µM, respectively) (Geisler et al., 2015), I3P was detected at ~80 µM (Dodd et al., 2017), and that IL4i1 is a secreted protein and active in the extracellular milieu, the protective concentrations of I3P and 4HPP are within a range to operate on neighboring cells, especially in limited perfusion cellular environments such as lymph nodes where numerous IL4i1-positive cells reside.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the experimental concentrations to physiological relevance.

claim: I3P has fluorescent properties that can be monitored using flow cytometry.
source: Therefore, we took advantage of the fluorescent properties of I3P to monitor its presence in the cells using flow cytometry (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Four hours after I3P removal, the cells reached fluorescence levels similar to control cells, indicating the deprivation of intracellular I3P.
source: Four hours after I3P removal, the cells reached fluorescence levels similar to control cells, indicating the deprivation of intracellular I3P.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the wash-out experiment shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Erastin upregulates SLC7A11 as a compensatory mechanism to elevate intracellular cysteine.
source: Erastin itself upregulates SLC7A11 (Dixon et al., 2014) as a compensatory mechanism to elevate intracellular cysteine.
evidence: This is stated as known information with a citation.

claim: 4HPP upregulated SLC7A11 and HO-1 in the presence of erastin.
source: In line, we also found 4HPP upregulated SLC7A11 and HO-1 in the presence of erastin (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: HO-1 was reported to have both detrimental and protective functions in ferroptosis.
source: HO-1 was reported to have both detrimental and protective functions in ferroptosis (Kwon et al., 2015; Chiang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as background information with citations.

claim: I3P and WT IL4i1 conditioned medium show concordance of differentially expressed genes.
source: Hierarchical clustering of significantly regulated genes showed concordance of differentially expressed genes in cells treated with I3P or medium containing the WT IL4i1 enzyme, whereas the gene expression in HeLa cells treated with medium containing the enzyme-dead mutant IL4i1 clustered with the untreated control (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Many of the overlapping genes upregulated by I3P and WT IL4i1 are associated with Nrf2 and AhR signaling.
source: Indeed, more than 90% of the most significantly upregulated genes (adjusted p-value<10−9) upon I3P treatment overlapped with the most significantly upregulated genes by WT IL4i1 (Figure 6B) – many of them representing target genes of Nrf2 and AhR signaling, and involved in oxidative stress protection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAseq data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: WT IL4i1 conditioned medium caused a dose dependent increase in I3P uptake by cells.
source: Moreover, monitoring I3P fluorescence via flow cytometry, we detected a dose dependent increase in the AmCyan fluorescence in cells treated with WT IL4i1-conditioned medium, but not in cells treated with the enzyme-dead mutant, confirming that IL4i1-generated I3P was taken up by the cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6C.

claim: WT IL4i1 conditioned medium caused a dose-dependent increase in HO-1 and SLC7A11.
source: In line with our previous findings, we observed this to be linked to a dose-dependent increase in HO-1 and SLC7A11 (Figure 6D), which was absent when using the control medium or the K351A mutant enzyme (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: The protective effect of IL4i1 was retained in medium containing human plasma concentrations of amino acids and glucose.
source: Since amino acid concentrations in cell culture medium do not reflect the physiological levels, we verified that the protective effect of IL4i1 was also retained in medium containing human plasma concentrations of amino acids and glucose as described by Leney-Greene et al., 2020; Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The venom LAAO does not induce ferroptosis.
source: In concordance with our previous observations regarding ferroptosis protection we confirmed that the venom LAAO does not induce this mode of cell death (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G.

claim: PP had no protective effect against ferroptosis.
source: Indeed, while PP had no protective effect, we found I3P suppressed ferroptosis in a titratable way (Figure 4B,C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which was accompanied by significantly decreased lipid peroxidation measured with C11-BODIPY (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 4B,C.
